notices.short_title: RFP Public Education Campaign Services for the New York City Charter Revision Commission
notices.description:
New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC) invites firms to submit a proposal in response to this Request for Proposals (RFP), to provide public education campaign services to maximize public awareness of New York City Charter ballot items. In May 2026, Mayor Mamdani announced the appointment of the Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE), a Charter Revision Commission tasked with making City government work better for New Yorkers. COGE is a body of 15 members and staffed by City of New York employees charged with reviewing the New York City Charter for potential revisions. The Commission held ten hearings across the five boroughs over the summer, released its interim report on July 3, 2026, and released its final report on July 23, 2026. NYCEDC is seeking a firm to provide public education campaign services, design and ad buys across multiple types of media, to maximize public awareness of the ballot items. The public education campaign will launch no later than September 15, 2026

NYCEDC plans to select a consultant on the basis of factors stated in the RFP  wh…

notices.description:
The Department of Homeless Services (DHS') is seeking appropriately qualified contractors/vendors to contract for the provision of shelter services for families with children, adult families, and single adults who are temporarily housed in DHS contracted commercial hotels. The selected vendors will provide services as outlined in this RFP to assist clients with their daily needs and to help them move out of the shelter system as quickly as possible.

The mission of DHS is to prevent homelessness when possible and to provide short-term emergency shelter for individuals and families who have no other housing options available. DHS primarily meets this goal by providing services to clients in long-term contracted purpose-built shelters throughout the City. When there are not enough available shelter beds and units in traditional shelters, DHS temporarily uses commercial hotels to house clients while they transition to permanent housing.  

Over the last 15 years, DHS has faced numerous crises which have forced DHS to rely on commercial hotels to temporarily house clients. Long term DHS is committed to phasing out the use of commercial hotels.  However, until such time t…
notices.plain: The Department of Homeless Services awarded Midway Living Inc a $67,796,535 contract to provide shelter and daily-needs services for families, adult families and single adults housed in contracted commercial hotels, selected through competitive proposals from a pre-qualified list.

notices.description: DYCD is seeking a qualified vendors to provide Advance & Earn programs in New York City. The populations served by the programs that are the subject of this NAE are adults that are seeking qualified organizations to provide new education and workforce development programs for opportunity youth (young adults ages 16-24 who are not in school and not working). Advance & Earn will help further their career through comprehensive High School Equivalency (HSE) test preparation, employer-recognized trainings, credentials and certifications, and paid internships. The program will combine services currently offered through DYCDs Young Adult Literacy Program (YALP) and Intern & Earn (formerly Young Adult Internship Program [YAIP]). The new programs will offer a continuum of education and employment services from literacy instruction through advanced training and job placement or college enrollment supported by comprehensive support services tailored to individual needs.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Goddard Riverside Community Center a $5.7 million contract, through a negotiated acquisition, to run Advance & Earn education and job-training programs for New Yorkers ages 16 to 24 who are neither in school nor working.

notices.description: To combat gun violence funding has been allocated to Saturday Night Lights (SNL) programing in areas where there has been an increase in crime. SNL is a youth development program that activated spaces throughout the city to provide free high-quality sports and fitness training for youth aged 11-18. These New York City neighborhoods identified based on the analysis of crime data and TRIE neighborhood review. Some located near where the precinct is listed in the top 30 precincts with the highest shootings in New York City.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Kids in the Game LLC a $64,104 contract through negotiated acquisition, with one or a few vendors, to run Saturday Night Lights youth sports and fitness programs in neighborhoods with rising crime, including areas near high-shooting precincts.

notices.description: The program offers free, student-centered, academically rigorous, and culturally responsive experiences for youth who completed kindergarten through eighth grade in the prior school year.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Chinese American Parents Association Inc a $262,811 contract through negotiation with a limited group of vendors, rather than open competition, to run free summer programs for students who finished kindergarten through eighth grade.

notices.description:
In accordance with section 3-04(b)(2)(i)(D) of the Procurement Policy Board Rules, the Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) intends to negotiate the Comprehensive After-School System (COMPASS) Center Based Programs. The COMPASS Center Based Programs provides after-school services tailored to 6-8 Middle school youth. COMPASS offers high quality programs that have a strong balance of academics, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of youth. COMPASS aims to help young people build skills to support their academic achievement, raise their confidence and cultivate their leadership skills through service learning and other civic engagement opportunities.

The term of this contract extension shall be for period of September 1, 2026, to August 31, 2027, with a one-year option to renew.
notices.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development intends to negotiate with a limited set of providers for after-school programs for middle school students, under a contract extension running Sept. 1, 2026, to Aug. 31, 2027, with a one-year renewal option.

notices.description:
EMERGENCY EXECUTIVE ORDER No. 2.41

 

July 29, 2026

 

WHEREAS, pursuant to a state of emergency first declared by Emergency Executive Order No. 224, dated October 7, 2022, and subsequent orders extending such state of emergency, the City has operated Humanitarian Emergency Response and Relief Centers to provide temporary housing in response to the substantial increase in new arrivals during recent years; and

 

WHEREAS, such orders issued prior to January 5, 2026 did not provide or require a plan for actions that would be taken to eliminate the need for the suspensions and modifications of laws and rules effected by the orders; and
notices.plain: The Office of the Mayor issued Emergency Executive Order No. 2.41, dated July 29, 2026, tied to a state of emergency over temporary housing at Humanitarian Emergency Response and Relief Centers for new arrivals.

Some located near where the precinct is listed in the top 30 precincts with the highest shootings in New York City.
notable.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Kids in the Game LLC a $64,104 contract through negotiated acquisition, with one or a few vendors, to run Saturday Night Lights youth sports and fitness programs in neighborhoods with rising crime, including areas near high-shooting precincts.

notable.short_title: Automated Training Roster Management Software Subscription
notable.description: The New York City Department of Correction seeks to procure a commercially available, subscription based automated training roster management software solution to support the Department's training administration, attendance tracking, roster management, and training completion documentation needs.
notable.plain: The Department of Correction awarded Compulink Technologies Inc a $50,400 contract for subscription software to manage training rosters, track attendance and document training completion, through a small purchase from a certified minority- or women-owned business without competition.

notable.short_title: Amendment of Rule Relating to Surcharge on Certain Non-Primary Residences - Extension of Time to File and Expansion of Processes - Emergency Rule
notable.plain: The Department of Finance has adopted an emergency rule amending its rules on the surcharge for certain non-primary residences, extending the time to file and expanding the processes covered.

notable.description:
In accordance with section 3-04(b)(2)(i)(D) of the Procurement Policy Board Rules, the Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) intends to negotiate the Comprehensive After-School System (COMPASS) Center Based Programs. The COMPASS Center Based Programs provides after-school services tailored to 6-8 Middle school youth. COMPASS offers high quality programs that have a strong balance of academics, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of youth. COMPASS aims to help young people build skills to support their academic achievement, raise their confidence and cultivate their leadership skills through service learning and other civic engagement opportunities.

The term of this contract extension shall be for period of September 1, 2026, to August 31, 2027, with a one-year option to renew.
notable.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development intends to negotiate with a limited set of providers for after-school programs for middle school students, under a contract extension running Sept. 1, 2026, to Aug. 31, 2027, with a one-year renewal option.
